From a04f0017c22453613d5f423326b190c61e3b4f98 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@imgtec.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2018 18:00:43 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] mmc: jz4740: Fix race condition in IRQ mask update

A spinlock is held while updating the internal copy of the IRQ mask,
but not while writing it to the actual IMASK register. After the lock
is released, an IRQ can occur before the IMASK register is written.
If handling this IRQ causes the mask to be changed, when the handler
returns back to the middle of the first mask update, a stale value
will be written to the mask register.

If this causes an IRQ to become unmasked that cannot have its status
cleared by writing a 1 to it in the IREG register, e.g. the SDIO IRQ,
then we can end up stuck with the same IRQ repeatedly being fired but
not handled. Normally the MMC IRQ handler attempts to clear any
unexpected IRQs by writing IREG, but for those that cannot be cleared
in this way then the IRQ will just repeatedly fire.

This was resulting in lockups after a while of using Wi-Fi on the
CI20 (GitHub issue #19).

Resolve by holding the spinlock until after the IMASK register has
been updated.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://github.com/MIPS/CI20_linux/issues/19
Fixes: 61bfbdb85687 ("MMC: Add support for the controller on JZ4740 SoCs.")
Tested-by: Mathieu Malaterre <malat@debian.org>
Signed-off-by: Alex Smith <alex.smith@imgtec.com>
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/mmc/host/jz4740_mmc.c b/drivers/mmc/host/jz4740_mmc.c
index 712e08d9a45e..a0168e9e4fce 100644
--- a/drivers/mmc/host/jz4740_mmc.c
+++ b/drivers/mmc/host/jz4740_mmc.c
@@ -362,9 +362,9 @@ static void jz4740_mmc_set_irq_enabled(struct jz4740_mmc_host *host,
 		host->irq_mask &= ~irq;
 	else
 		host->irq_mask |= irq;
-	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&host->lock, flags);
 
 	writew(host->irq_mask, host->base + JZ_REG_MMC_IMASK);
+	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&host->lock, flags);
 }
 
 static void jz4740_mmc_clock_enable(struct jz4740_mmc_host *host,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/mmc/host/jz4740_mmc.c`**
- The code modification involves the placement of the `spin_unlock_irqrestore` function call. 
- Originally, the spinlock was released before the `writew` function call that updates the `IMASK` register. 
- The patch moves the `spin_unlock_irqrestore` call to after the `writew` function, ensuring that the spinlock is held during the entire process of updating the internal IRQ mask and writing it to the `IMASK` register.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a race condition that could occur if an IRQ is triggered after the internal IRQ mask is updated but before the `IMASK` register is written. By holding the spinlock until after the `IMASK` register is updated, the patch prevents the possibility of stale values being written to the register, which could lead to unhandled IRQs and system lockups, particularly affecting Wi-Fi functionality on the CI20 device. This change ensures that the IRQ mask update is atomic and consistent, thereby improving the stability of the system.

A spinlock is held while updating the internal copy of the IRQ mask,
but not while writing it to the actual IMASK register. After the lock

then we can end up stuck with the same IRQ repeatedly being fired but
not handled. Normally the MMC IRQ handler attempts to clear any
unexpected IRQs by writing IREG, but for those that cannot be cleared

This was resulting in lockups after a while of using Wi-Fi on the

Resolve by holding the spinlock until after the IMASK register has

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://github.com/MIPS/CI20_linux/issues/19
Fixes: 61bfbdb85687 ("MMC: Add support for the controller on JZ4740 SoCs.")
Tested-by: Mathieu Malaterre <malat@debian.org>
Signed-off-by: Alex Smith <alex.smith@imgtec.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by a race condition where the spinlock is released before the `IMASK` register is updated. This allows an IRQ to occur after the internal IRQ mask is modified but before the actual register is written, potentially leading to stale values being written to the `IMASK` register. If the IRQ that occurs cannot be cleared by writing to the `IREG` register, it can result in repeated unhandled IRQs and system lockups.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void jz4740_mmc_set_irq_enabled(struct jz4740_mmc_host *host,
 	unsigned int irq, bool enabled)
 {
 	unsigned long flags;
 
 	spin_lock_irqsave(&host->lock, flags);
 	if (enabled)
 		host->irq_mask &= ~irq;
 	else
 		host->irq_mask |= irq;
-	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&host->lock, flags);
 
 	writew(host->irq_mask, host->base + JZ_REG_MMC_IMASK);
+	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&host->lock, flags);
 }
